text: Before enlightenment, chop wood, carry water.|After enlightenment, chop wood, carry water.
What was your face before your parents were born?
The moon does not consider whether|she is reflected in the water.
If you understand, things are just as they are.|If you do not understand, things are just as they are.
Not knowing is most intimate.
The way is not difficult|for those who have no preferences.
When you get there, there is nowhere to arrive.
The snow falls, each flake|in its appropriate place.
Sitting quietly, doing nothing,|spring comes and the grass grows by itself.
The wild geese do not intend to cast their reflection.|The water has no mind to receive their image.
The flower invites the butterfly with no-mind.|The butterfly visits the flower with no-mind.
Mountains are mountains.|Water is water.
The pine tree does not know|it is teaching you patience.
The candle flame does not mourn what it has burned.
This very place is the lotus land.|This very body, the Buddha.
Spring flowers, autumn moon, summer breeze, winter snow.|With a clear, uncluttered mind,|every season is a good season.
Carrying water, I am the water.|Carrying wood, I am the wood.
The finger pointing at the moon|is not the moon.
The oak tree does not wait for permission|to become an oak tree.
The river does not refuse the fallen leaf.
Nothing is hidden.|Everything has always been here.
Still water reflects the mountain|exactly as it is.
The flower does not compare itself to other flowers.
The turtle carries its home|without calling it a burden.
The stone does not try to be still.|It simply is.
The cloud does not decide|which direction to travel.
One moon shows in every pool.|In every pool, one moon.
All rivers lead to the sea.|The sea is never full.
The old pond.|A frog jumps in.|Sound of water.
The wind does not move.|The flag does not move.|Your mind moves.
The candle does not know that it gives light.|That is why it gives light.
The bird leaves no trace in the air.|The fish leaves no trace in the water.
Muddy water,|let stand,|becomes clear.
The dewdrop slides off the lotus leaf|without leaving a trace.
The deep river does not boast of its depth.
Born from emptiness,|returning to emptiness,|playing in the in-between.
Nothing remains but a single moon|reflected in the cold water.
The seed does not struggle to become the tree.
The forest is silent.|The tree falls.|The forest is silent.
The mind is like the moon on water.|Handle it too roughly and the image is gone.
The silence between two notes|is also music.
Consider the lotus:|rooted in mud,|blooming in light.
The flame does not ask why it is warm.
The mountain does not move.|Therefore it arrives everywhere.
Soft water|wears away hard stone.|Be soft water.
Before thinking, what are you?
You cannot see your own eyes without a mirror.|You cannot know your own mind without stillness.
Where were you before the universe began?
What is the colour of wind?
Where does the flame go|when the candle is blown out?
The eye through which I see the universe|is the same eye through which|the universe sees me.
Before the first thought, what are you?
If not now, when?|If not here, where?
The gate is open.|Why do you stand at the threshold?
Between yes and no,|how much distance is there?
To study the self is to forget the self.
The present moment always will have been.
The ten thousand things|arise and return|to the one.
To know that you do not know|is knowing.
All is impermanent.|That too is impermanent.
Why are you looking outside?|You are the source.
Realise the silence that is your true nature.
What is there before the first thought?
The drum has never beaten itself.|Who is the one who hears?
Not two. Not one.
Just this.
You are the sky.|Everything else is just the weather.
This moment will not return.|That is what makes it precious.
Between the tick and the tock,|where do you live?
What you are looking for|is what is looking.
Each moment contains|a thousand years of silence.
Nothing is missing.
If you cannot find the truth right where you are,|where else do you expect to find it?
Let the moment be what the moment is.
Expect nothing.|Be ready for everything.
Not speaking, not silent.
You are not a drop in the ocean.|You are the ocean in a drop.
The present moment is the only home|there has ever been.
Does a dog have Buddha-nature?|Mu.
Three pounds of flax.
Walk on.
Empty your cup.
Wash your bowl.
When the iron cow moos, listen.
Knock on the sky and listen to the sound.
Form is emptiness.|Emptiness is form.
Rest and be taken.
Be a lamp unto yourself.
Do not seek the truth.|Only cease to cherish your opinions.
The gate of heaven is open|but the gateless gate is closer.
A gate that cannot be passed through|is not a gate at all.
Even the longest journey|begins with a single step|already taken.
If you are facing in the right direction,|all you need to do is keep walking.
The journey of a thousand miles|begins beneath your feet.
To a beginner there are many possibilities.|To an expert there are few.
What is the sound of one hand?
Even in the depths of winter|I know that within me|there is an invincible summer.
A student asked: What is the greatest miracle?|The master poured tea and said:|That you are here to ask.
A student asked: What is emptiness?|The master opened his hand.
A student asked: What is Zen?|The master poured tea until the cup overflowed.
Have you eaten your breakfast?|Yes.|Then go wash your bowl.
A monk asked: What is Buddha?|The master replied: Three pounds of flax.|The monk stood in silence.|The master drank his tea.
A student asked: What happens after death?|The master said: I don't know.|But you are a master!|Yes. But not a dead one.
The master said: Before enlightenment I was depressed.|After enlightenment I was still depressed.|But the depression was two inches shorter.
A student asked: What is Zen?|The master slapped him.|The student was grateful.
If you meet the Buddha on the road, kill him.
You cannot step into the same river twice.|The river agrees.
